summary: Elmer Henry Cutts was an indologist and historian who earned his B.A. from the University of Washington and his Ph.D. from Harvard. He held posts at Washington, Tufts, and Northeastern University, and founded Andhra University in 1958.
Elof Olesen was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed an M.A. at the University of Copenhagen between 1895 and 1903, studying under Michael Viggo Fausbøll.

Elpidius Pax studied linguistics and religious studies at Breslau under Wilhelm Havers and Otto Strauss, later earning degrees at Munich and the Pontifical Institute. He held posts at Leipzig University Library, Studium Biblicum Franciscanum, and Dormition Abbey.

Else Lüders was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. She studied under Heinrich Lüders between approximately 1900 and 1941 and received an honorary Dr. phil. from the University of Rostock in 1919.

Else Pauly was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Copenhagen under Louis Trolle Hjelmslev and Poul Tuxen. She served as a part-time lecturer in Pāli at the University of Copenhagen from 1973 to 1979.

Else Wohlgemuth worked in Indology and sinology. She studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, the University of Marburg, and the University of Leipzig, where she earned her Ph.D. under Ernst Windisch by 1916.

Emanuel Sarkisyanz was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of Tehran and completed his Ph.D. at the University of Chicago. In 1967, he served as Head at Heidelberg University.

Emanuela Garatti is a Tibetologist who completed a doctorate at the École Pratique des Hautes Études. She held a post at the University of Munich (attested 2018) and served as ATER at the EPHE in 2022.

Embar Krishnamacharya was an Indologist. He held posts as an editor for Gaekwad's Oriental Series (attested 1926), Pandit at the Oriental Manuscripts Library, and at Sanskrit Pathashala, Vadtal (attested 1937) and Sanskrit Mahavidyalaya, Vadodara (attested 1939).

Emi Matsushita worked in history and archaeology, earning degrees from Nanzan University, the University of East Anglia, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. She taught for Shizuoka Prefectural Board of Education and was a graduate assistant at OSU.

Emil Abegg, an Indology and religious studies scholar, studied at Zurich and Leipzig under Adolf Kaegi, Ernst Windisch, Eduard Sievers, and August Conrady. He was a Privatdozent and then Professor at the University of Zurich from 1928 to 1955.
Emil Ernst Strohal was an Indologist who studied at Graz, Vienna, and Leipzig under Johann Kirste, Georg Bühler, and Ernst Windisch, earning his Ph.D. at Göttingen under Franz Kielhorn in 1900.

Emil Franke was an Indologist who studied at Charles University, the University of Vienna, and Humboldt University of Berlin, completing his doctoral studies under Josef Zubatý. He later held a post at the National Library of the Czech Republic.

Emil Rödiger was a scholar in linguistics and religious studies who earned his Dr. phil. and Lic. theol. from Halle-Wittenberg. He became a full professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1835–1860) and ordentlicher Professor at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1860.

Emil Schlagintweit was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied law at Humboldt University of Berlin and with tutor Franz Joseph Lauth. He served as a Bavarian Regierungsrat and was a member of the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.

Emil Schmidt worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Jena, Leipzig, Bonn, and Humboldt University of Berlin (M.D. ~1861), he served at the University of Leipzig as Privatdozent (1885), ao. Professor of Ethnology (1890), and Honorarprofessor (1896).

Emil Sieg was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Berlin, Tübingen, and Munich under Franz Kielhorn and others, he took up a Lehrstuhl at the University of Göttingen in 1920.

Emile Joseph Dillon was a scholar of linguistics, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied across several institutions, earning degrees from Saint Petersburg, KU Leuven, and the University of Kharkiv, where he became a professor in 1884.

Emilio Bartoli, a scholar of Indology and linguistics, studied under Michele Kerbaker. He taught Latin and Greek at Liceo Classico Statale Vittorio Emanuele II and was Docente of comparative grammar and Sanskrit at the University of Naples Federico II (1923–1925).

Emilio Lovarini studied at the University of Padua (~1885–1889), specializing in Indology and other fields. He served as Docent of Italian Literature at the University of Bologna in 1900 and taught at Liceo Ginnasio Luigi Galvani and Liceo Artistico di Bologna.
